# Repair draft (step 4) and AC integrity gate

## Proposed replacement body

```markdown
## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. Today, 95% of exports of the representative 100-row report finish within 5s (the p95 export latency). This figure comes from the recorded request-timing run.

## Problem
Requesters wait up to 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export. The required maximum is 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Using the representative 100-row report, request CSV exports and measure request-to-file-ready latency with the same request-timing method as the recorded 5s p95 baseline: p95 latency is <= 2s.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.
```

**Changes from the original:**
- **AC no longer names an environment.** "In staging" was removed under the deploy-window rule. The AC row now gives setup, action, and observable result, and the spec picks the venue.
- **Measurement folded into the AC.** The `Measurement clarification` section is not a permitted body section. Its method (same request-timing method, representative 100-row report, request-to-file-ready latency) now sits inside the AC row. Its provenance note ("supplied values, not estimates") is reflected in Context, which cites the recorded run.
- **p95 defined in plain words.** Context now explains the term at first use.
- **Preserved unchanged:**
  - target (2s)
  - baseline (5s)
  - the Idea sketch line
  - the non-blocking Post-deployment housekeeping

**Proposed comment:** none.
- The Idea is already a single attributed sketch line, so nothing overflows from it.
- Nothing displaced from Context or Problem matches the step-5 closed list.
- No overlap evidence or in-session ask exists.
- The measurement text moved into the AC, so it was not demoted.

This is a body-only write.

## AC integrity gate (on the assembled draft)

**Normalization:** the single criterion is already a `- [ ]` item. Nothing to extract.

| AC | Class test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| p95 latency <= 2s for the representative 100-row CSV export | Comparative. It needs a baseline, a target, and a measurement, all nameable today. | **Pass.** Baseline: 5s p95, from the recorded request-timing run, supplied rather than guessed. Target: <= 2s. Measurement: the same request-timing method, request-to-file-ready latency, on the representative 100-row report. |

- **Deploy-window:** pass. The AC can be fulfilled with a pre-prod run on representative data. The environment name is removed.
- **Post-deployment:** "monitor export latency after release" is prod-only. It stays in Post-deployment housekeeping as non-blocking and is not an AC. The AC list is not emptied.
- **Wishful / tautological:** none, so no hard stop.
- **Unspecified-but-binding / external-input:** none, so no park. The ticket stays ready.

**Gate outcome:** clean. The draft proceeds to the step-5 deterministic gates.

## Proposed replacement body

## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. The current p95 export latency is 5s for the representative 100-row report, measured in the recorded request-timing run. The recorded baseline and required 2s target are supplied values, not estimates.

## Problem
Requesters wait 5s at p95 for a 100-row CSV export instead of the required maximum of 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when CSV exports are requested and request-to-file-ready latency is measured using the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline, p95 export latency is <= 2s, compared with the recorded baseline of 5s.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.

---

**AC integrity gate: PASS.** The criterion preserves the supplied baseline, target, and measurement method, and names the setup, action, and observable result. It is verifiable before production deployment; staging is removed from the criterion because the spec selects the verification venue. Post-release monitoring remains explicitly non-blocking housekeeping.

**Proposed comment:** none; no detail was displaced.
